outcome: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study enrolled 62 pregnant women with singleton breech presentations at or beyond 37 weeks of gestation who underwent ECV, along with a control group of 12 women with cephalic presentations.
finding: External cephalic version (ECV) is an effective intervention for reducing cesarean delivery rates in breech presentations, with its success being significantly associated with lower maternal BMI, prior vaginal delivery, non-posterior placental location, higher amniotic fluid index, and fewer procedural attempts.
mod_finding: The ECV success group achieved a significantly higher vaginal delivery rate (81%) and a lower cesarean delivery rate (19%) compared to the ECV failure group.
followup_time: Up to delivery, with no long-term follow-up data mentioned for maternal and neonatal outcomes.
birth_weight: Average 3266.4 g in the ECV success group and 3063.2 g in the failure group.
gest_age: At or beyond 37 weeks of gestation
